identity.name: CENTRAL BANK OF INDIA
identity.industry: Public Sector Bank (PSU bank — RAM-led lending, high CASA)

summary.oneLiner: A turnaround PSU bank posting strong headline growth and improving asset quality, the corporate-book optics are flattered by a very low base

one-line thesis: A turnaround PSU bank posting strong headline growth (global business +18%, advances +28.6%) and improving asset quality (GNPA 2.60%, credit cost 0.40%), with 14.9% ROE and 3.06% NIM; the corporate-book optics are flattered by a very low base, and the key watch-item is the phased ECL transition (from 1-Apr-2027) and sustaining ~3% quarterly loan growth to hit full-year guidance.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global business | INR 8,33,320 cr | +18.29% | Deposits INR 4,78,972 cr (+11.68%); CASA 46.61% |
| Gross global advances | INR 3,54,348 cr | +28.58% | Corporate +46.52% (low base); RAM +21.38%; QoQ advance growth only ~2.85% |
| Net interest income | INR 3,914 cr | +15.70% | NIM 3.06% (>3% guidance) |
| Net profit | INR 1,324 cr | +13.26% | Highest-ever quarterly; ROA 1%, ROE 14.92% (from 14.17%) |
| Operating profit | INR 2,186 cr | n/d | (management said "for the financial year" — read as the quarter) |
| Total income | INR 10,678 cr | +3.08% | Cost of deposit 4.60% (−33 bps) |
| GNPA / NNPA | 2.60% / 0.49% | GNPA −53 bps | PCR ~95.86%; slippage 0.29% (−6 bps); credit cost 0.40% (from 0.68%) |
| CRAR / CET1 | 18.28% / 16.24% | — | Tier-1 16.54%; LCR moderated to 156% (from 235/210%); NSFR 128% |
> Advance growth 28.6% YoY is inflated by corporate low base (INR 76,966 cr → INR 1,12,770 cr); QoQ growth only ~2.85%. RAM:Corporate mix 68:32 vs 65:35 (±5%) guidance.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Deposit growth 11–12%**, **advances growth 14–16%** for FY27; quarter-on-quarter loan growth ~3%.
- **NIM ≥3%**, **ROA ≥1%** maintained; **yield on advances 7.89% → ~8% by Mar-2027** (gold/SHG mix shift).
- **Cost-to-income** to fall **1.5–1.6%** over the coming year (target <56%; currently 55.40%).
- **ECL** provisioning: INR 1,525 cr (Stage 1&2) already made of ~INR 4,500–5,000 cr total requirement; **shift to ECL from 1-Apr-2027**; ~80 bps CRAR impact if taken at once (can stagger over 5 yrs).
- **No equity capital raise** despite board approval to raise up to INR 7,000 cr (equity/AT-1) — "enough capital."
- **FCNR(B)**: USD 8.4 mn mobilised; targeting **USD 400 mn by Sep-2026**.
- Recovery from technical write-off book: **INR 2,200–2,500 cr this FY** (INR 500 cr targeted this quarter).
- GIFT City: **USD 200 mn deposit + USD 500 mn trade book** over next few years.
order book & pipeline: - Undisbursed corporate advances ~INR 5,000 cr; New Business Group meets weekly. Corporate pipeline in renewable energy, data centres, HAM (roads), CRE. ECLGS 5.0: INR 4,646 cr sanctioned / INR 3,693 cr disbursed. SARFAESI: 600–700 property sales targeted this FY (vs 460 last FY).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Bancassurance** — ~26% in Generali Central Life & Non-Life (INR 627 cr invested); prior year was establishment stage, now stabilised, good income expected FY27.
- **GIFT City IFSC unit** — inaugurated 29-Jun-2026; leverage for overseas/NRI/forex business.
- New verticals board-approved: **wealth management, credit card, NRI, marketing** — bank is re-entering credit cards (8.33 cr customer base).
- Dedicated **Gold Loan** (book ~INR 36,000 cr) and **SHG** divisions created under an ED.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Gold loan + SHG** as yield-accretive growth engines (yield 8%+), with South India expansion runway.
- **Fee income build-out** — centralised BG cell + centralised forex cell; 159 NRI desks; 35 customer-acquisition centres; 9 government-business centres; 300 marketing officers + 1,000 trained credit officers (join first week Oct-2026).
- **Cross-sell** products (Cent Queen INR 1,457 cr; Salary Cent Prestige INR 787 cr) as platforms for vehicle/housing/car loans.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: - **CASA franchise 46.61%** and **85% of term deposits <INR 3 cr** (retail, sticky) — a low-cost, granular liability base underpinning cost of deposit at 4.60%. 65% of the 4,605-branch network is rural/semi-urban (RUSU), delivering 58% priority-sector achievement vs 40% mandate — a structural PSL and low-cost-deposit advantage.
margins & cost dynamics: - NIM 3.06%; cost of deposit 4.60% (−33 bps, "stabilised"; term deposits mostly repriced). Yield on advances 7.89% (from 7.78%), guided to ~8%. Cost-to-income 55.40% — targeting <56% with 1.5–1.6% reduction via fee-income growth + cost curtailment (ATM/currency-chest/utility optimisation).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Branch/vertical expansion: new corporate-finance & mid-corporate branches planned; GIFT City ramp. 1,000 credit officers deploy from Oct-2026. No large physical capex flagged.
capital allocation: - CRAR 18.28% / CET1 16.24% — self-sufficient; board approval to raise up to INR 7,000 cr kept as an unused option ("no plan as of now"). Deliberately running down excess LCR (235%→156%) and lifting CD ratio (64%→74%) to deploy idle liquidity into higher-return advances. INR 627 cr in insurance JVs.
risks & watch-items:
- **ECL transition (1-Apr-2027)** — INR 4,500–5,000 cr total need vs INR 1,525 cr provided; ~80 bps CRAR hit if front-loaded.
- Headline advance growth (+28.6%) is **low-base optics** on corporate; sustaining ~3% QoQ is the real test.
- Sharp LCR (235→156%) and NSFR (147→128%) drawdown — deliberate but reduces buffer.
- Agriculture KCC slippage (INR 200 cr) and pending farm **debt-waiver scheme** dynamics.
- Legacy recovery dependence (technical write-off book INR 32,900+ cr; old aviation account — INR 515 cr CGTMSE guarantee received, land parcel re-auction in August).
- Execution risk on new verticals (credit card, wealth) and fee-income ramp.
management quality / tone: - Confident, granular, guidance-anchored MD (Kalyan Kumar) — repeatedly frames growth vs stated guidance and stresses underwriting/monitoring quality. Candid that corporate growth is low-base-driven and that KCC/agri is the slippage source. Emphasis on efficiency (business/branch INR 185 cr, business/employee INR 24 cr). Overall credible turnaround narrative.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The +28.6% advance-growth headline is largely a corporate low-base artefact; RAM (+21%) is the durable engine and the bank itself down-weights the corporate optic.
- Management is intentionally consuming its liquidity buffer (LCR/NSFR down, CD ratio up) as a margin/return lever — a deliberate balance-sheet-efficiency call, not stress.
- Board-approved INR 7,000 cr raise is being held in reserve, not used — a signalling option; ECL is the real reason to keep capital high.
- Corporate pipeline explicitly tilts to renewable energy + data centres + HAM roads — Central Bank is a lender-beneficiary of those capex themes.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis:
| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| ECL/expected-loss transition from 1-Apr-2027 | Well-provided PSU banks incl. CENTRALBK · 532885 | Thinly-provided lenders | INR 1,525 cr already set aside; ~80 bps manageable hit. Med |
| Corporate credit demand in renewables, data centres, HAM roads | CENTRALBK · 532885 (lender) | — | Explicit pipeline tilt; low corporate base = runway. Med |
| Gold-loan formalization / South India penetration | CENTRALBK · 532885 (new gold-loan division) | — | Yield-accretive (8%+); INR 36,000 cr book with headroom. Med |
| Farm-loan debt-waiver scheme (agri KCC slippage) | — | CENTRALBK · 532885 (agri book) | INR 200 cr KCC slippage; waiver adds uncertainty. Low–Med |
| RBI (1-Jul) intraday-funding change for brokers | Banks incl. CENTRALBK · 532885 | Brokers needing self-funded margin | Brokers must now arrange own margin money. Low |

- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Global business INR 8,33,320 cr (+18.29%); advances +28.58% (corporate +46.52% low base, RAM +21.38%); net profit INR 1,324 cr (+13.26%, highest-ever); NIM 3.06%, ROA 1%, ROE 14.92%; GNPA 2.60%/NNPA 0.49%, credit cost 0.40%, slippage 0.29%; CRAR 18.28%/CET1 16.24%; CD ratio 74.10% (from 64%); LCR 156% (from ~210–235%). business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Strong Brand Image with Legacy of 114+ Years" and "Strong Rural + Semi Urban Presence with 65% of Total Branches in RUSU Centers".
- "Best CASA base @46.61% of Total Deposits" (the deck's own wording); CASA % moved 46.88% (Jun'25) to 46.61% (Jun'26), a stated (27 bps) change.
- "Pan India Presence with 22346 Customer Touch Points out of which 85% is in RUSU Centers"; active customer base 8.33 Crore; dedicated staff strength 34125.
- Government of India holds 81.19% as on 30th June 2026; shares are listed on BSE and NSE and are part of NSE 500, BSE 500 and BSE PSU indices.
- Values framework 'CENTRAL' (Consistency, Ethical Standards, Nurturing Potential, Transparency, Responsiveness, Accountability, Loyalty) with the FY26-27 theme "YEAR OF BUSINESS EXCELLENCE".

- _Next Q → check: QoQ loan growth holding ~3% and full-year 14–16% advances / 11–12% deposits; NIM ≥3%; yield-on-advances march to 8%; cost-to-income toward <56%; ECL top-up cadence; FCNR(B) toward USD 400 mn (Sep); write-off recoveries toward INR 2,200–2,500 cr; credit-card/wealth vertical launch._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Guidance scorecard FY26-27] The deck publishes targets against Jun'26 achievement: Business Growth 14-15% (18.29%), Deposit Growth 10-12% (11.68%), Advances Growth 14-16% (28.58%), CASA 48% (+/-1%) (46.61%), RAM:Corporate 65:35 (+/-5%) (68:32), NIM Above 3% (3.06%), Gross NPA Below 2.50% (2.60%), Net NPA Below 0.50% (0.49%), PCR 96-98% (95.86%), Slippage Ratio less than 0.25% Q-o-Q (0.29%), Credit Cost (Annualized) upto 0.75% (0.40%), ROA 1% and above (1.00%), Cost to Income <56% (55.40%).
- [Asset quality] Gross NPA % trend 3.13 / 3.01 / 2.70 / 2.67 / 2.60 and Net NPA % 0.49 / 0.48 / 0.45 / 0.49 / 0.49 across Jun'25 to Jun'26; sector GNPA % at Jun'26 is Agriculture & Allied 5.82, MSME 5.19, Retail 1.00, Corporate & Others 0.65.
- [Provision coverage] The PCR chart carries two unlabelled series, 97.02/96.88/96.69/95.97/95.86 and 84.86/84.55/83.80/81.86/81.41 across Jun'25-Jun'26; only the first is confirmed as PCR by the guidance table (95.86% at Jun'26), so the second series is not attributed here.
- [Restructured book] Total standard restructured book fell to Rs 3818 Cr at Jun'26 from Rs 4948 Cr at Jun'25; SMA accounts of Rs 5 Crore and above total Rs 850 Cr (0.24% of global advance) at Jun'26 vs Rs 1008 Cr (0.37%) at Jun'25, of which Rs 17.89 Cr is common between SMA and Restructured Accounts.
- [Group structure] Subsidiaries Cent Bank Home Finance Ltd. (64.40%, housing finance, present in 12 States through 38 branches and 3 SPOKE locations, advances & investment portfolio of Rs 1816.08 Cr) and Centbank Financial Services Ltd. (100%, trusteeship); associates Generali Central Life Insurance (25.27%) and Generali Central Insurance (24.91%) — both "became the associates effective June 05, 2025" and both posted Jun'26 quarter losses of Rs (56.94) Cr and Rs (88.92) Cr respectively — plus Indo Zambia Bank Limited, Zambia (20%) with Jun'26 quarter net profit of Rs 154.62 Cr.
- [One-off tax item] FY Mar'26 ROE of 13.00%, EPS of Rs 4.83 and ROA of 0.89% are footnoted as "After taking one time impact of recognition of Deferred Tax Asset at 25.168% as against 34.944% amounting to Rs 632 Crore".
- [Treasury duration risk] Modified duration of the AFS book lengthened to 5.47 at Jun'26 from 3.67 at Jun'25 (SLR MD 5.85 vs 3.75) and PV01 (SLR+NSLR) rose to 19.62 from 14.76; HTM share of the investment book rose to 73.51% from 68.82%.
- [Award] "Recognized as the 'Most Preferred Workplace 2026-27' by Marksmen Daily".
